properties.content:
Report Details

Incident Type: FIXED

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: TECK ALASKA INC.
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 67.566540, -162.966197 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 0.5 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT***APPROXIMATELY TWO QUARTS OF HYDRAULIC FLUID WAS SPILLED ON THE DRILL DECK OF ONE OF THE HELICOPTER FLY RIGS THAT IS BEING USED BY TECK AMERICAN TO EXPLORE IN THE SU VALLEY. MOST OF THE SPILLED HYDRAULIC FLUID REMAINED ON THE DRILL DECK. SOME OF THE HYDRAULIC FLUID LEAKED THROUGH THE SEAMS OF THE DECKING AND DRIPPED ONTO THE TUNDRA. WE DON’T BELIEVE THAT MORE THAN 10 TO 20 DROPS OF HYDRAULIC FLUID DRIPPED ONTO THE TUNDRA. WE HAVE PLACED ABSORBENT PADS AROUND THE PERIMETER OF THE DRILL PAD TO PREVENT THE HYDRAULIC FLUID FROM SPREADING OUT FROM UNDER THE DRILL PAD. ONCE THE WEATHER CLEARS AND ALLOWS US TO RETURN TO THE DRILL SITE, WE WILL REMOVE THE DECKING TO CLEAN UP HYDRAULIC FLUID THAT HAS LEAKED UNDER THE DRILL RIG DECKING.

ORIGINAL REPORT: CALLER REPORTED AN ACCIDENT INVOLVING AT LEAST ONE VEHICLE RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN FERTILIZER. A SECONDARY TANK NEARBY CONTAINED A PLACARD READING UN 1789. IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE TANK THAT RUPTURED CONTAINS THE SAME MATERIAL OR IF A HOSE CONNECTED TO THE RUPTURED TANK ALSO CONNECTS TO THE SECONDARY TANK.

properties.title: NRC Report: Oil, Misc: Lubricating in Narr near New London, NC
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 1022136 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: ALCOA
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1022136
Incident Time: 2012-08-24 10:45:00
Nearest City: New London, NC
Location: ALCOA HYDROPOWER FACILITY- TUCKERTOWN LOCATION 711 TUCKERTOWN RD
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: OIL, MISC: LUBRICATING
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ALCOA
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 35.489751, -80.121604 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 8 gallons
Report Description
ON 8/24/12 AT APPROXIMATELY 10:45 AM ONE OF THE ALCOA EMPLOYEES NOTIFIED ME THEY WERE CLEANING THE THRUST BEARING HEAT EXCHANGER FOR UNIT 2 DURING ROUTINE MAINTENANCE AND NOTICED THAT WHEN THEY PULLED THE ROD OUT OF THE TUBE OIL CAME OUT. IT LOOKED LIKE OVER TIME THE WALLS HAD GOTTEN THIN AND WHEN THE DEBRIS WAS REMOVED IT RUPTURED THE TUBE WHICH ALLOWED THE OIL TO LEAK INTO THE WATER JACKET. THE OIL IN THE THRUST BEARING SUMP WAS ML 680 AND THE WATER DISCHARGES INTO OUTFALL 002 SO I HAD THEM TO CHECK THE TAILRACE FOR AN OIL SHEEN. THE EMPLOYEE REPORTED BACK THE HE THOUGHT IT LOOKED LIKE THERE MAY BE A SHEEN. WE CONTACTED DISPATCH AND HAD THEM SHUT DOWN UNIT 3, WHICH THEY JUST STARTED AND TOOK ALL 3 UNIT AT TUCKERTOWN OUT OF SERVICE TO PREVENT THE SHEEN FROM SPREADING. I NOTIFIED THE ALCOA CREW AT HIGH ROCK AND HAD THEM HEAD TO TUCKERTOWN TO HELP WITH THE CONTAINMENT AND CLEANUP. THIS WAS THEN REPORTED INTERNALLY WITHIN ALCOA AND CLEAN-UP WAS INITIATED. WE LAUNCHED OUR BOAT AND BEGAN DEPLOYING BOOMS. THE WIND WAS BLOWING UP RIVER AND PUSHED THE OIL TO THE DAM WHICH AIDED IN THE CLEANUP. WE USED TWO 100’ BOOMS MADE UP OF OIL ABSORBENT PADS TO CONTAIN AND COLLECT THE SHEEN. WE ALSO USED HTP TO COLLECT THE OIL AND REMOVE THE SHEEN FROM THE WATER. THE WAS ACCOMPLISHED BY BROADCASTING THE HTP INTO THE WATER AND ALLOWING IT TO COLLECT ANY OIL ON THE WATER AND WE DIPPED THE HTP OUT WITH NETS AND PLACED THE CONTAMINATED DEBRIS INTO DRUMS. THE CLEANUP WAS COMPLETED AT 4:00 PM AND NO SHEEN WAS VISIBLE ON THE WATER. UNIT 1 AND 3 WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE AND UNIT 2 WAS TAGGED OUT FOR REPAIRS. APPROXIMATELY 8 GALLONS OF OIL WAS CLEANED UP ON THE SURFACE OF THE WATER.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.723889, -73.866944 (Approximated from Explicit )
Reported Spill Volume: 2 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** WHILE LOADING DRUMS AND PALLETIZE CUBIC YARD BOXES ONTO TRAILER, DRIVER PROCEEDED FORWARD TOO FAR ALLOWING FORKS TO PUNCTURE LOWER PORTION OF ONE DRUM. APPROXIMATELY 2-3 GALLONS OF LIQUID WAS RELEASED IN BACK OF TRAILER. THE DRIVER IMMEDIATELY NOTICED THE SPILL AND NOTIFIED OTHERS OF THE INCIDENT. ABSORBANT MATERIAL WAS PUT DOWN TO CONTAIN THE SPILL AND THE DRUM WAS LAYED DOWN ON ITS SIDE TO PREVENT MORE LEAKAGE. THE HOLE WAS PLUGGED WITH DRUM PUTTY AND THEN PLACED IN AN OVER-PACK DRUM ALONG WITH THE CLEANED-UP ABSORBANT MATERIAL. NO LIQUID EXITED THE VEHICLE AND THE SPILL WAS CLEANED UP IN APPROXIMATELY 1/2 HOUR. THERE WERE NO INJURIES. ALL FORK TRUCK DRIVERS WILL BE RETRAINED AND THIS INCIDENT WILL BE SPECIFICALLY DISCUSSED.

properties.summary: Incident Type: PIPELINE - NRC Report ID: 881791 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party:
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 881791
Incident Time: 2008-08-21 19:40:00
Nearest City: Sugar Creek, MO
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 1-D
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party:
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 40 gallons
ON AUGUST 8, 2008 A FIELD TECHNICIAN IDENTIFIED THAT A DENSITOMETER PUMP NEEDED REPAIR WHEN HE NOTICED PRODUCT COMING FROM A WEEP HOLE IN THE PUMP BODY. HE IMMEDIATELY SHUT OFF THE PUMP AND ISOLATED IT USING 1" BALL VALVES ON THE INLET AND OUTLET OF THE PUMP. AT THAT TIME MANHOLE COVERS OVER THE FRENCH DRAIN WERE REMOVED AND HE INSPECTED FOR CONTAMINATION. NO CONTAMINATION WAS FOUND. LATER, DURING ROUTINE SAMPLING AT THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR, ALLOWABLE POTW CONCENTRATIONS WERE EXCEEDED. THE ANALYTICAL RESULTS WERE BROUGHT TO MANAGEMENT ATTENTION, PROMPTING INVESTIGATION. APPROXIMATELY 30 GALLONS OF DIESEL WERE COLLECTED FROM THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR. THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR IS FED BY THE FACILITY FRENCH DRAIN, LEADING US TO BELIEVE THE DIESEL HAD MIGRATED TO IT FROM THE DENSITOMETER PUMP, WHICH IS LOCATED IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO IT. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT APPROXIMATELY 40 GALLONS OF DIESEL HAD BEEN RELEASED.

LATER, DURING ROUTINE SAMPLING AT THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR, ALLOWABLE POTW CONCENTRATIONS WERE EXCEEDED. THE ANALYTICAL RESULTS WERE BROUGHT TO MANAGEMENT ATTENTION, PROMPTING INVESTIGATION. APPROXIMATELY 30 GALLONS OF DIESEL WERE COLLECTED FROM THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR. THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR IS FED BY THE FACILITY FRENCH DRAIN, LEADING US TO BELIEVE THE DIESEL HAD MIGRATED TO IT FROM THE DENSITOMETER PUMP, WHICH IS LOCATED IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO IT. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT APPROXIMATELY 40 GALLONS OF DIESEL HAD BEEN RELEASED.

Nearest City: OK
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: CONDENSATE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: DCP MIDSTREAM
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 42 gallons
REPORTING PARTY WAS NOTIFIED BY LANDOWNER ON 2/5/2009 AT APPROXIMATELY 16:15 THAT ONE OF OUR NATURAL GAS GATHERING LINES WAS LEAKING AND MADE ITS WAY INTO AN UNNAMED, NON-FLOWING CREEK. REPORTING PARTY PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON-SITE WITHIN 90 MINUTES OF LANDOWNER NOTIFICATION AND ESTIMATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 1 BARREL OF NATURAL GAS LIQUIDS, OR CONDENSATE, HAD BEEN RELEASED FROM A 4" PVC GATHERING LINE. THE CONDENSATE FLOWED ABOUT 50 FEET TO A POOLED AREA OF WATER, BUT THE CREEK IS MOSTLY DRY. THE AFFECTED AREA IS APPROXIMATELY 80' X 7' AND THE CONDENSATE IS ON TOP OF THE WATER. AFFECTED AREA HAS BEEN CONTAINED AND TEMPORARY FENCING PLACED AROUND LEAK AREA. IN THE MORNING, PUMP TRUCKS WILL VACUUM UP CONDENSATE/WATER MIXTURE AND ADDITIONAL REMEDIATION MEASURES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AFTER FURTHER EVALUATION.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Port Arthur, TX
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: BUTADIENE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: FLINT HILLS RESOURCES
Skytruth Analysis
OPERATIONS NOTICED ODORS COMING FROM THE PROPYLENE REFLUX DRUM AREA IN THE LOU. UPON INVESTIGATING, ON 12/15/09 AT 21:30 HOURS, OPERATIONS DISCOVERED THAT A VALVE WAS OPEN AND ALLOWING VAPORS TO BACKFLOW FROM THROUGH THE VALVE AND TO THE ATMOSPHERE. THE VALVE WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUT TO STOP THE EMISSIONS. INITIALLY, IT WAS BELIEVED THAT THE VAPOR SOURCE WAS FROM THE PROPYLENE REFLUX DRUM AND CONSISTED OF MAINLY PROPYLENE. INITIAL RELEASE QUANTITIES FROM THIS SCENARIO INDICATED THAT NO REPORTABLE QUANTITIES HAD BEEN EXCEEDED. HOWEVER, ON 12/16/09 AT APPROXIMATELY 17:30 HRS, ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WAS DISCOVERED TO INDICATE THAT THE VAPORS WERE ACTUALLY BACKFLOWING FROM THE LOU FLARE HEADER. EMISSION CALCULATIONS WERE IMMEDIATELY PERFORMED FOR THIS SCENARIO AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT AT REPORTABLE QUANTITY FOR 1,3 BUTADIENE HAD BEEN EXCEEDED.

IT DID HAVE SHARP EDGES AND A HIGH CONTRAST AGAINST THE SURROUNDING OCEAN SURFACE. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE COMING FROM THE NNE BETWEEN 10-15 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: NONE.
